archetype.name: Retooling Year (stuck in the middle)
archetype.definition: A third straight season with a negative run differential and a record within a few games of .500: real pieces in the infield and the middle of the order, but not enough around them to threaten a division that Milwaukee ran away with.

report.headline: Above .500 through June, then July's 10-18 sank a glove-first, thin-bullpen team

recap.finish: 77-85, fourth in the NL Central, 26 games behind MIL; missed the postseason
recap.body:
The 2026 Cardinals were close to exactly what their runs said they were. They scored 720 and allowed 749. That works out to -0.18 per game, 18th in the league, and a W vs Run Diff of -1.1 says they won about one game fewer than that margin implied. No bad luck story is hiding here. This was a slightly below-average team that played like one. The shape underneath is more interesting: a top-five defense (23.1 Fielding Runs, 5th), a lineup whose B- grade beats its 28th-ranked .691 OPS, and a pitching staff whose 4.26 ERA looks worse once you remember the home park plays at 94.

For three months the formula held. A 15-11 April put them at 18-13, May broke even, and a 13-12 June left them 44-38 at the end of the month, six games over .500. They never got hot: the longest winning streak all year was six games. July undid it. A 10-18 month on a modest -10 run margin dropped them to 54-56, and they never climbed back. August was a wash at 14-14. September was 9-15, with 5.17 runs allowed per game, the worst run prevention of any month. They finished 2-8 over the last ten, including a three-game sweep in Milwaukee to close the year.

The offense ran through three bats. Alec Burleson (125 wRC+, 26 HR, 116 RBI, 3.2 WAR) and Jordan Walker (119 wRC+, 29 HR, 22 SB) supplied nearly all the thump. Iván Herrera's .353 OBP from the DH spot earned an All-Star nod despite a .382 slugging mark. The 17th-ranked scoring offense outperformed the OPS because the park suppresses everything. But the bottom of the order gave a lot back: Nolan Gorman (62 wRC+, -0.5 WAR in 302 PA), Pedro Pagés (65), and corner outfielders Nathan Church (81) and José Fermín (86) combined for over 1,300 plate appearances of below-average hitting.

The team's best player was a glove. JJ Wetherholt led the club with 4.6 WAR, built mostly on 18.1 Def Runs at second base, and ranked 2nd of 56 on the 2B tab. Masyn Winn added 13.3 Def Runs at short, enough to make a 78 wRC+ season worth 2.3 WAR. Behind that infield, the rotation graded a C. Kyle Leahy (3.66 ERA, 3.59 FIP) and Andre Pallante (3.83, 3.74) were solid. Michael McGreevy ate 168.2 innings while striking out just 16.4% of hitters. Matthew Liberatore's 5.23 ERA and 1.47 WHIP over 155 innings were the soft spot. The bullpen graded a D, and the reason is walks. George Soriano (12.1%), Ryne Stanek (12.0%), Gordon Graceffo (11.0%) and closer Riley O'Brien (10.5%, 38 saves, 4.08 ERA) all walked more than one hitter in ten.

In context, this was a lateral move. The run differential improved from -0.40 in 2025 to -0.18, and the defense from 18.0 to 23.1 Fielding Runs. But OPS was flat (.693 to .691), and the close-game luck that had padded the 2024 (+7.0) and 2025 (+3.7) records ran out. The result was one fewer win and a drop from 19th to 22nd on the site. They finished 12 games behind the second-place Cubs.

highlights.title: Elite middle-infield defense
highlights.body: Wetherholt and Winn combined for 31.4 Def Runs and drove a team Fielding Runs total that ranked 5th. Defense is why Wetherholt led the club in WAR despite a 101 wRC+, and why Winn was still a 2.3-WAR player with a 78. Fielding has been positive four straight years, so this looks like a real organizational trait rather than noise.

highlights.title: Burleson and Walker anchored the lineup
highlights.body: The two carried a lineup that otherwise struggled to slug. Burleson posted a 125 wRC+ with 116 RBI, and Walker hit 29 homers with 22 steals. Both played 158+ games, so availability was part of their value. They are the reason the hitter group graded B- despite a bottom-three team OPS.

highlights.title: Leahy and Pallante steadied the rotation
highlights.body: Both starters backed sub-4.00 ERAs with FIPs to match (3.59 and 3.74), so their run prevention wasn't fluky. Together they gave 302 innings and 5.3 WAR, the most dependable part of the staff.

lowlights.title: A walk-prone bullpen
lowlights.body: The relief corps graded a D. Every one of the five heaviest-used relievers except Justin Bruihl walked more than 10% of batters, Soriano and Stanek above 12%. Graceffo's 2.67 ERA sits well under his 3.79 FIP, so even the best-looking number in the group is likely to regress.

lowlights.title: Dead weight at the lineup's bottom
lowlights.body: Gorman, Pagés, Church and Fermín took over 1,300 plate appearances, all with a wRC+ of 86 or lower. That's the main reason team OPS ranked 28th. The core three can't cover four lineup spots producing at that level, and nothing in the history suggests the lineup is trending up on its own, since OPS has slid from .745 in 2022 to .691.

lowlights.title: The July collapse
lowlights.body: A 10-18 July turned a 44-38 team into a sub-.500 one. The month's run margin was only -10, so close losses magnified it. September's 9-15 and a 2-8 finish sealed it, with run prevention at its worst down the stretch.

arc.note: Steady and slightly above .500 through June (44-38), then a 10-18 July and a 9-15 September dragged them to 77-85, ending with a sweep at Milwaukee.

recap.nextYear: The numbers leave a clear foundation and clear holes. Wetherholt's defense, Winn's glove, and the Burleson-Walker middle of the order are the carryover, along with Leahy and Pallante as rotation stabilizers whose FIPs back their ERAs. The work is at the bottom of the lineup, where four regulars hit well below average, and in a D-graded bullpen that walks too many hitters to protect leads. Liberatore's 5.23 ERA is also a problem, though his 4.62 FIP and 22.8% strikeout rate suggest some of it was bad fortune. Luck isn't the excuse this time: the record matched the run differential almost exactly. That cuts both ways, since the 2024-25 records had been inflated by close-game breaks. A third straight negative run differential says this roster, as built, is a .480 team that needs real upgrades rather than better bounces.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; record and run differential agree.
